links.effect: ChatGPT-4o varied across centers (Center 2 89.0% vs Center 4 78.0%, P=0.032); DeepSeek-V3 showed no significant difference across centers (P=0.114).
links.quote: Additionally, ChatGPT-4o exhibited significant variability across centers, particularly between Center 2 and Center 4 (89.0% vs. 78.0%, P=0.032), whereas DeepSeek-V3 showed no such difference.

links.outcome: Extraction performance under varied input and prompting conditions across heterogeneous report styles
links.effect: Performance varied by lesion count and field; the models had lower accuracy on numerical information expressed in Chinese. Each report was tested once, so reproducibility across repeated runs was not assessed.
links.quote: In addition, the LLMs showed relatively lower accuracy in extracting numerical information expressed in Chinese, suggesting additional challenges in handling linguistic variability.

links.outcome: Overestimation of report-level extraction accuracy owing to predominance of negative fields
links.effect: Report-level success fell from 85.4% to 75.9% (DeepSeek-V3) and from 83.3% to 73.4% (ChatGPT-4o) when only positive fields were assessed.
links.quote: In the sensitivity analysis ( Table S4 ), the report-level extraction success rates decreased to 75.9% (607/800) for DeepSeek-V3 and 73.4% (587/800) for ChatGPT-4o.
